title: CBSE Class 12 Mathematics · Practice paper 3
subject: Mathematics
label: Practice paper
instr: This question paper contains 38 questions. All questions are compulsory.
This question paper is divided into five Sections - A, B, C, D and E.
In Section A, Questions no. 1 to 18 are multiple choice questions (MCQs) and Questions no. 19 and 20 are Assertion-Reason based questions of 1 mark each.
In Section B, Questions no. 21 to 25 are Very Short Answer (VSA) type questions, carrying 2 marks each.
In Section C, Questions no. 26 to 31 are Short Answer (SA) type questions, carrying 3 marks each.
In Section D, Questions no. 32 to 35 are Long Answer (LA) type questions, carrying 5 marks each.

In Section E, Questions no. 36 to 38 are case study based questions carrying 4 marks each. The first two case study questions have three sub-parts (i), (ii), (iii) of 1, 1 and 2 marks; the third has two sub-parts of 2 marks each.

There is no overall choice. However, an internal choice has been provided in 2 questions in Section B, 3 questions in Section C, 2 questions in Section D and one sub-part each in 2 questions of Section E.
Draw neat and clean figures wherever required. Take π = 22/7 wherever required, if not stated.
Use of calculators is not allowed.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The principal value of $\cot^{-1}(-\sqrt{3})$ is
questions.sol: The principal value branch of $\cot^{-1}$ is $(0,\pi)$. $\cot\frac{5\pi}{6}=-\cot\frac{\pi}{6}=-\sqrt{3}$ and $\frac{5\pi}{6}\in(0,\pi)$, so the value is $\frac{5\pi}{6}$.

questions.sol: $\operatorname{cosec}^{-1}x$ takes values in $\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$ except 0, since $\operatorname{cosec}$ is not defined at 0.

questions.sol: Let $\sin^{-1}\frac{3}{5}=\theta$, so $\sin\theta=\frac{3}{5}$ with $\theta\in\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$; here $\theta$ is in the first quadrant. $\cos\theta=\sqrt{1-\frac{9}{25}}=\frac{4}{5}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The value of $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1}xe^{x}\,dx$ is
questions.sol: By parts: $\int xe^{x}dx=xe^{x}-e^{x}$. So $\left[xe^{x}-e^{x}\right]_{0}^{1}=(e-e)-(0-1)=1$.

questions.sol: $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{e^{x}}{e^{y}}\Rightarrow e^{y}dy=e^{x}dx$. Integrating: $e^{y}=e^{x}+C$.

questions.text: The vectors $2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$ and $\lambda\hat{i}+6\hat{j}-8\hat{k}$ are collinear if $\lambda$ is equal to
questions.sol: Collinear vectors have proportional components: $\frac{\lambda}{2}=\frac{6}{-3}=\frac{-8}{4}=-2$, so $\lambda=-4$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are non-zero vectors such that $|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|=|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|$, then $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are
questions.sol: Squaring: $|\vec{a}|^{2}+2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}+|\vec{b}|^{2}=|\vec{a}|^{2}-2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}+|\vec{b}|^{2}\Rightarrow\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=0$, so the vectors are perpendicular.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Which of the following points lies in the feasible region determined by the constraints $x+2y\le 8$, $3x+y\le 9$, $x\ge 0$, $y\ge 0$?
questions.sol: $(2,2)$: $2+4=6\le 8$ and $6+2=8\le 9$, so it satisfies all the constraints. $(3,1)$ gives $3x+y=10\gt 9$; $(0,5)$ gives $x+2y=10\gt 8$; $(1,4)$ gives $x+2y=9\gt 8$.

questions.text: A bag contains 4 red and 6 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random one after the other without replacement. The probability that both balls are red is
questions.sol: By the multiplication theorem: $P=\frac{4}{10}\times\frac{3}{9}=\frac{12}{90}=\frac{2}{15}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the function $f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac{\sin 5x}{3x}, & x\neq 0\\ k, & x=0\end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=0$, then the value of $k$ is
questions.sol: $\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\sin 5x}{3x}=\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{5}{3}\cdot\frac{\sin 5x}{5x}=\frac{5}{3}$. For continuity, $k=f(0)=\frac{5}{3}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): $y=\sin x$ is a solution of the differential equation $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}-y=0$.
Reason (R): $y=e^{x}$ is a solution of the differential equation $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}-y=0$.
Select the correct option.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.sol: For $y=\sin x$: $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}-y=-\sin x-\sin x=-2\sin x$, which is not zero for all $x$, so A is false. For $y=e^{x}$: $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}-y=e^{x}-e^{x}=0$, so R is true.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): For the vectors $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}$, $|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|=2$.
Reason (R): $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=-(\vec{b}\times\vec{a})$ for any two vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$.
Select the correct option.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.sol: $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k}\\ 1 & 1 & 0\\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{vmatrix}=-2\hat{k}$, so $|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|=2$: A is true. R is a true property of the vector product, but it does not give the value in A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find $\displaystyle\int x\sec^{2}x\,dx$.
questions.model:
Integrating by parts, taking $x$ as the first function:
$\int x\sec^{2}x\,dx=x\tan x-\int 1\cdot\tan x\,dx=x\tan x-\log|\sec x|+C$
$=x\tan x+\log|\cos x|+C$

points.t: Correct use of integration by parts: $x\tan x-\int\tan x\,dx$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: For any two vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ with $|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|$, show that $\vec{a}+\vec{b}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{a}-\vec{b}$. Verify this for $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$.
questions.model:
$(\vec{a}+\vec{b})\cdot(\vec{a}-\vec{b})=|\vec{a}|^{2}-\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}+\vec{b}\cdot\vec{a}-|\vec{b}|^{2}=|\vec{a}|^{2}-|\vec{b}|^{2}=0$, so $\vec{a}+\vec{b}\perp\vec{a}-\vec{b}$ (when both are non-zero).
Verification: $|\vec{a}|=\sqrt{4+1+4}=3$ and $|\vec{b}|=\sqrt{1+4+4}=3$.
$\vec{a}+\vec{b}=3\hat{i}+3\hat{j}$, $\vec{a}-\vec{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$, and $(\vec{a}+\vec{b})\cdot(\vec{a}-\vec{b})=3-3+0=0$.

or.text: Find the direction cosines of the line passing through the points $A(1, 2, -3)$ and $B(3, -4, 0)$. Also show that this line is perpendicular to a line whose direction ratios are $3, 1, 0$.
or.model:
Direction ratios of AB: $3-1, -4-2, 0+3$, i.e. $2, -6, 3$. $\sqrt{4+36+9}=7$.
Direction cosines: $\frac{2}{7}, -\frac{6}{7}, \frac{3}{7}$
$2(3)+(-6)(1)+3(0)=0$, so the two lines are perpendicular.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A coin is tossed three times. Let $E$ be the event 'exactly two heads are obtained' and $F$ be the event 'the first toss shows a head'. Find $P(E|F)$. Are the events $E$ and $F$ independent? Give a reason.
questions.model:
Sample space: 8 equally likely outcomes. $E=\{HHT, HTH, THH\}$, so $P(E)=\frac{3}{8}$. $F=\{HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT\}$, so $P(F)=\frac{4}{8}=\frac{1}{2}$.
$E\cap F=\{HHT, HTH\}$, so $P(E\cap F)=\frac{2}{8}=\frac{1}{4}$.
$P(E|F)=\frac{P(E\cap F)}{P(F)}=\frac{1/4}{1/2}=\frac{1}{2}$
Since $P(E|F)=\frac{1}{2}\neq\frac{3}{8}=P(E)$ (equivalently $P(E\cap F)=\frac{1}{4}\neq P(E)P(F)=\frac{3}{16}$), $E$ and $F$ are not independent.

points.t: Not independent, since $P(E|F)\neq P(E)=\frac{3}{8}$ (or $P(E\cap F)\neq P(E)P(F)$)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Using determinants, find the area of the triangle whose vertices are $(1, 2)$, $(4, 6)$ and $(-2, 5)$. Also, using determinants, find the equation of the line joining the points $(1, 2)$ and $(4, 6)$.
questions.model:
Area $=\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 1\\ 4 & 6 & 1\\ -2 & 5 & 1\end{vmatrix}\right|=\frac{1}{2}\left|1(6-5)-2(4+2)+1(20+12)\right|=\frac{1}{2}|1-12+32|=\frac{21}{2}$ square units
Let $(x, y)$ be any point on the line. The three points are collinear, so $\begin{vmatrix}x & y & 1\\ 1 & 2 & 1\\ 4 & 6 & 1\end{vmatrix}=0$
$x(2-6)-y(1-4)+1(6-8)=0\Rightarrow -4x+3y-2=0$
Equation of the line: $4x-3y+2=0$

questions.text: Find the intervals in which the function $f(x)=x^{4}-8x^{2}$ is (i) strictly increasing, (ii) strictly decreasing.
questions.model:
$f'(x)=4x^{3}-16x=4x(x-2)(x+2)$; $f'(x)=0\Rightarrow x=-2, 0, 2$
Sign of $f'(x)$: negative on $(-\infty,-2)$, positive on $(-2,0)$, negative on $(0,2)$, positive on $(2,\infty)$.
(i) $f$ is strictly increasing on $(-2,0)\cup(2,\infty)$.
(ii) $f$ is strictly decreasing on $(-\infty,-2)\cup(0,2)$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the particular solution of the differential equation $(x+1)\frac{dy}{dx}-y=e^{x}(x+1)^{2}$, $x\gt -1$, given that $y=1$ when $x=0$.
questions.model:
Dividing by $(x+1)$: $\frac{dy}{dx}-\frac{1}{x+1}y=e^{x}(x+1)$, a linear equation with $P=-\frac{1}{x+1}$, $Q=e^{x}(x+1)$.
I.F. $=e^{-\int\frac{dx}{x+1}}=e^{-\log(x+1)}=\frac{1}{x+1}$
Solution: $y\cdot\frac{1}{x+1}=\int e^{x}(x+1)\cdot\frac{1}{x+1}\,dx=e^{x}+C$, i.e. $y=(x+1)(e^{x}+C)$
$y(0)=1$: $1=1\cdot(1+C)\Rightarrow C=0$
Particular solution: $y=(x+1)e^{x}$

or.text: Find the particular solution of the differential equation $2xy\frac{dy}{dx}=x^{2}+3y^{2}$, $x\gt 0$, given that $y=1$ when $x=1$.
or.model:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{x^{2}+3y^{2}}{2xy}$ is homogeneous. Put $y=vx$, $\frac{dy}{dx}=v+x\frac{dv}{dx}$.
$v+x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{1+3v^{2}}{2v}\Rightarrow x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{1+v^{2}}{2v}\Rightarrow\frac{2v}{1+v^{2}}dv=\frac{dx}{x}$
Integrating: $\log(1+v^{2})=\log x+\log C\Rightarrow 1+v^{2}=Cx\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}=Cx^{3}$
$y(1)=1$: $2=C$
Particular solution: $x^{2}+y^{2}=2x^{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Show that the lines $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+1}{3}=\frac{z-2}{1}$ and $\frac{x-5}{2}=\frac{y-1}{-1}=\frac{z-6}{3}$ intersect. Also find their point of intersection.
questions.model:
A general point on the first line: $(2\lambda+1, 3\lambda-1, \lambda+2)$; on the second line: $(2\mu+5, -\mu+1, 3\mu+6)$.
For a common point: $2\lambda+1=2\mu+5\Rightarrow\lambda-\mu=2$ and $3\lambda-1=-\mu+1\Rightarrow 3\lambda+\mu=2$.
Solving: $\lambda=1$, $\mu=-1$.
Check the z-coordinates: $\lambda+2=3$ and $3\mu+6=3$. They are equal, so the lines intersect.
Point of intersection: $(3, 2, 3)$

or.text: Find the vector and cartesian equations of the line passing through the point $(2, -1, 3)$ and perpendicular to both the lines $\vec{r}=\lambda(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})$ and $\vec{r}=\mu(3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})$.
or.model:
The required line is parallel to $\vec{b}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})\times(3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k}\\ 1 & 2 & -1\\ 3 & -1 & 2\end{vmatrix}=3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-7\hat{k}$
Vector equation: $\vec{r}=(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+t(3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-7\hat{k})$
Cartesian equation: $\frac{x-2}{3}=\frac{y+1}{-5}=\frac{z-3}{-7}$

questions.text:
Solve the following linear programming problem graphically:
Maximise $Z=3x+4y$
subject to the constraints $2x+y\le 10$, $x+2y\le 8$, $x\ge 0$, $y\ge 0$.
questions.model:
Draw $2x+y=10$ (through $(5,0)$ and $(0,10)$) and $x+2y=8$ (through $(8,0)$ and $(0,4)$). The feasible region is the bounded region on the origin side of both lines in the first quadrant.
Intersection of the lines: $x=8-2y\Rightarrow 16-4y+y=10\Rightarrow y=2$, $x=4$.
Corner point$Z=3x+4y$
$(0,0)$0
$(5,0)$15
$(4,2)$20
$(0,4)$16
Maximum $Z=20$ at $x=4$, $y=2$.

points.t: Correct graph with the bounded feasible region shaded

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A=\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$, where $\mathbb{N}$ is the set of natural numbers, and let $R$ be the relation on $A$ defined by $(a,b)\,R\,(c,d)$ if and only if $a+2d=c+2b$. Show that $R$ is an equivalence relation. Also find the equivalence class of $(3,1)$.
questions.model:
Reflexive: for every $(a,b)\in A$, $a+2b=a+2b$, so $(a,b)\,R\,(a,b)$.
Symmetric: if $(a,b)\,R\,(c,d)$, then $a+2d=c+2b$, i.e. $c+2b=a+2d$, so $(c,d)\,R\,(a,b)$.
Transitive: if $(a,b)\,R\,(c,d)$ and $(c,d)\,R\,(e,f)$, then $a+2d=c+2b$ and $c+2f=e+2d$. Adding: $a+2d+c+2f=c+2b+e+2d\Rightarrow a+2f=e+2b$, so $(a,b)\,R\,(e,f)$.
Hence $R$ is an equivalence relation.
Equivalence class of $(3,1)$: $(c,d)\,R\,(3,1)\iff c+2=3+2d\iff c=2d+1$.
$[(3,1)]=\{(2d+1,d): d\in\mathbb{N}\}=\{(3,1),(5,2),(7,3),\ldots\}$

or.text: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=\frac{x}{x^{2}+1}$. Show that $f$ is neither one-one nor onto. Also find the range of $f$.
or.model:
Not one-one: $f(2)=\frac{2}{5}$ and $f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{1/2}{5/4}=\frac{2}{5}$. So $f(2)=f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$ but $2\neq\frac{1}{2}$.
Range: let $y=\frac{x}{x^{2}+1}$. Then $yx^{2}-x+y=0$.
If $y=0$, $x=0$. If $y\neq 0$, this quadratic in $x$ has a real root only when $1-4y^{2}\ge 0$, i.e. $-\frac{1}{2}\le y\le\frac{1}{2}$.
So the range of $f$ is $\left[-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}\right]$.
Not onto: the range is not the whole co-domain $\mathbb{R}$; for example, 1 has no pre-image.

points.t: Not one-one, with an example such as $f(2)=f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Evaluate: $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\sin 2x}{(1+\sin^{2}x)(3+\sin^{2}x)}\,dx$.
questions.model:
Put $t=\sin^{2}x$, so $dt=2\sin x\cos x\,dx=\sin 2x\,dx$. When $x=0$, $t=0$; when $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$, $t=1$.
$I=\int_{0}^{1}\frac{dt}{(1+t)(3+t)}$
Partial fractions: $\frac{1}{(1+t)(3+t)}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{1+t}-\frac{1}{3+t}\right)$
$I=\frac{1}{2}\left[\log(1+t)-\log(3+t)\right]_{0}^{1}=\frac{1}{2}\left[\log\frac{1+t}{3+t}\right]_{0}^{1}$
$=\frac{1}{2}\left(\log\frac{2}{4}-\log\frac{1}{3}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{3}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Using integration, find the area of the triangle whose vertices are $A(-1, 1)$, $B(1, 5)$ and $C(3, 3)$.
questions.model:
Equations of the sides:
AB: $y-1=\frac{5-1}{1+1}(x+1)\Rightarrow y=2x+3$
BC: $y-5=\frac{3-5}{3-1}(x-1)\Rightarrow y=6-x$
AC: $y-1=\frac{3-1}{3+1}(x+1)\Rightarrow y=\frac{x+3}{2}$
Area $=\int_{-1}^{1}\left[(2x+3)-\frac{x+3}{2}\right]dx+\int_{1}^{3}\left[(6-x)-\frac{x+3}{2}\right]dx$
$=\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{3x+3}{2}\,dx+\int_{1}^{3}\frac{9-3x}{2}\,dx$
$=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{3x^{2}}{2}+3x\right]_{-1}^{1}+\frac{1}{2}\left[9x-\frac{3x^{2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{3}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{9}{2}+\frac{3}{2}\right)+\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{27}{2}-\frac{15}{2}\right)=3+3$
Area $=6$ square units

points.t: Equations of AB, BC and AC: $y=2x+3$, $y=6-x$, $y=\frac{x+3}{2}$
Correct integrals with limits $-1$ to 1 and 1 to 3 (with sketch)

or.text: Using integration, find the area of the region in the first quadrant bounded by the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{16}+\frac{y^{2}}{9}=1$, the x-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=2$.
or.model:
In the first quadrant, $y=\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{16-x^{2}}$.
Area $=\int_{0}^{2}\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{16-x^{2}}\,dx=\frac{3}{4}\left[\frac{x}{2}\sqrt{16-x^{2}}+\frac{16}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac{x}{4}\right]_{0}^{2}$
$=\frac{3}{4}\left[\frac{2}{2}\sqrt{12}+8\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{2}\right]=\frac{3}{4}\left[2\sqrt{3}+\frac{4\pi}{3}\right]$
$=\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}+\pi$ square units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Bag I contains 4 white and 2 black balls, and Bag II contains 3 white and 5 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random from Bag I, without replacement, and put into Bag II. Then one ball is drawn at random from Bag II.
(i) Find the probability that the ball drawn from Bag II is white.
(ii) If the ball drawn from Bag II is white, find the probability that both the balls transferred were white.
questions.model:
Let $E_1$: both transferred balls are white; $E_2$: one white and one black; $E_3$: both black. Let $W$: the ball drawn from Bag II is white.
$P(E_1)=\frac{^{4}C_{2}}{^{6}C_{2}}=\frac{6}{15}$, $P(E_2)=\frac{4\times 2}{15}=\frac{8}{15}$, $P(E_3)=\frac{1}{15}$
After the transfer Bag II has 10 balls: $P(W|E_1)=\frac{5}{10}$, $P(W|E_2)=\frac{4}{10}$, $P(W|E_3)=\frac{3}{10}$
(i) $P(W)=\frac{6}{15}\cdot\frac{5}{10}+\frac{8}{15}\cdot\frac{4}{10}+\frac{1}{15}\cdot\frac{3}{10}=\frac{30+32+3}{150}=\frac{65}{150}=\frac{13}{30}$
(ii) By Bayes' theorem, $P(E_1|W)=\frac{P(E_1)P(W|E_1)}{P(W)}=\frac{30/150}{65/150}=\frac{30}{65}=\frac{6}{13}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
In an adventure park, a straight zip-line cable runs from the top of a platform at the point $A(1, 2, 8)$ to an anchor at the point $B(5, 6, 0)$ on the ground. Distances are in metres, with respect to a fixed origin. The top of a lamp post is at the point $P(6, 1, 4)$, and a second straight cable passes through the points $C(0, 1, 2)$ and $D(2, 5, 4)$.
Based on the given information, answer the following questions:

parts.q: (i) Find the length of the cable AB.
(ii) Write the cartesian equation of the line AB.
parts.model: Direction ratios of AB: $4, 4, -8$, i.e. $1, 1, -2$. Equation: $\frac{x-1}{1}=\frac{y-2}{1}=\frac{z-8}{-2}$

parts.q: (iii) Find the foot of the perpendicular from the top of the lamp post P to the cable AB, and the length of this perpendicular.
parts.model:
A general point on AB: $Q(\lambda+1, \lambda+2, 8-2\lambda)$. $\overrightarrow{PQ}=(\lambda-5)\hat{i}+(\lambda+1)\hat{j}+(4-2\lambda)\hat{k}$.
$\overrightarrow{PQ}\perp AB$: $(\lambda-5)+(\lambda+1)-2(4-2\lambda)=0\Rightarrow 6\lambda-12=0\Rightarrow\lambda=2$
Foot of the perpendicular: $Q(3, 4, 4)$; length $PQ=\sqrt{(3-6)^{2}+(4-1)^{2}+(4-4)^{2}}=3\sqrt{2}$ m

or.q: (iii) Find the angle between the cable AB and the second cable CD.
or.model:
Direction ratios of CD: $2-0, 5-1, 4-2$, i.e. $2, 4, 2$, or $1, 2, 1$. Direction ratios of AB: $1, 1, -2$.
$\cos\theta=\frac{|1(1)+1(2)+(-2)(1)|}{\sqrt{6}\sqrt{6}}=\frac{1}{6}$, so $\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A drone is programmed so that its height above the ground, $t$ seconds after a timer starts, is $h(t)=t^{3}-12t^{2}+36t+10$ metres, for $0\le t\le 7$.
Based on the given information, answer the following questions:

parts.q: (i) Find the rate at which the height is changing at $t=1$ s.
(ii) At what times is the vertical speed of the drone zero?
(iii) Using the second derivative test, find the local maximum and local minimum heights of the drone.

points.t: $h''(t)=6t-24$ with the correct signs at $t=2$ and $t=6$
Local maximum height 42 m and local minimum height 10 m

or.q: (iii) Find the time intervals in which the drone is rising and in which it is coming down.
or.model:
$h'(t)=3(t-2)(t-6)$. For $0\lt t\lt 2$, $h'(t)\gt 0$; for $2\lt t\lt 6$, $h'(t)\lt 0$; for $6\lt t\lt 7$, $h'(t)\gt 0$.
The drone is rising during $(0, 2)$ and $(6, 7)$ and coming down during $(2, 6)$.

points.t: Rising in $(0, 2)$ and $(6, 7)$; coming down in $(2, 6)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Three snack stalls X, Y and Z at a school fair sell cups of tea, samosas and sandwiches. The numbers sold in one day are:
Stall X: 30 cups of tea, 20 samosas, 10 sandwiches
Stall Y: 25 cups of tea, 15 samosas, 20 sandwiches
Stall Z: 40 cups of tea, 30 samosas, 5 sandwiches
The selling prices are ₹10 for a cup of tea, ₹15 for a samosa and ₹40 for a sandwich. The cost prices are ₹6, ₹10 and ₹30 respectively.
Based on the given information, answer the following questions:

parts.q: (i) Write the sales matrix $S$ (rows X, Y, Z; columns tea, samosa, sandwich) and the column matrix $P$ of selling prices, and find the revenue of each stall using matrix multiplication.
(ii) Using matrices, find the profit of each stall and the total profit of the three stalls.
parts.model:
Profit per item: $P-C=\begin{bmatrix}10-6\\ 15-10\\ 40-30\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\ 5\\ 10\end{bmatrix}$
$S(P-C)=\begin{bmatrix}120+100+100\\ 100+75+200\\ 160+150+50\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}320\\ 375\\ 360\end{bmatrix}$
Profit: X ₹320, Y ₹375, Z ₹360; total profit = ₹1055

points.t: Profit per item matrix $\begin{bmatrix}4\\ 5\\ 10\end{bmatrix}$ (or cost matrix $SC$)
